sections.overview: Porcellio dilatatus is a terrestrial woodlouse native to southwestern Europe and introduced in many other regions.
sections.identification: It is broad-bodied, flattened and rough, and females can reach about 20 mm. Its rounded telson helps distinguish it from the pointed telson of P. scaber.
sections.habitat: It often lives close to people, including compost or manure heaps and stables, but records also come from some natural habitats.
sections.diet: Like other woodlice, it feeds on decaying plant material; species-specific diet details are limited in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Its frequent presence in buildings and manure or compost piles reflects a tolerance for human-modified habitats.
sections.reproduction: In females, fertilization is associated with ovarian maturation and the brood-related molt, as shown in physiological work on this species.
sections.ecology: P. albinus is a burrowing isopod of sandy desert habitats. P. dilatatus is instead frequently recorded around human settlements.
sections.conservation: No global conservation assessment is reported in the regional and taxonomic sources consulted.
